To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) joint axis orientation and joint angle modulation range and frequency are crucial for the workspace and acuity of insect antennae, (ii) joint axis orientation is crucial for the efficiency of tactile sampling, and (iii) the stick insect's movement strategy is optimal in terms of tactile efficiency for a wide range of edge directions, while the cricket's strategy is optimal only for horizontal edges.
the workspace and sampling acuities are determined by morphological properties of antennal joint axes and the range and frequency of joint angle modulations, respectively.

the workspace and sampling acuit of insect antennae are determined by the orientation and number of joint axes, while sampling performance is determined by the frequency and range of joint angle modulation and the predominant edge direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the basic principles of active sampling in tactile sensing.
the basic principles of active sampling of tactile information by antennae.
the basic principles of active sensing and their dependence on morphology and movement strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stick insect antenna performs better than the cricket antenna in a variety of environments.
the morphological and behavioural properties of the antenna, as well as the environment, are all important factors for tactile efficiency.
, in the absence of a specific environmental constraint, the optimal movement strategy is the one that maximizes the range of the antennal movement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the morphological properties of the antennae and the movement strategy of a single antenna have strong effects on tactile efficiency.
the morphology and movement strategy of insect antennae are tuned to the environment, and that the optimal strategy is not unique.
the stick insect is better equipped than the cricket to cope with environmental changes, but the cricket can sample more efficiently in the environment for which it was optimized.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to achieve a high sampling acuity and efficiency, the antennae must be designed to sample in the most efficient way, i.e. with the most suitable joint angle modulation frequencies and phase shifts.
a simple model of two hinge joints is able to explain a large part of the variation of tactile sampling performance observed across species.
the design of the antenna is crucial for the efficiency of tactile sensing.
